 How to Use Your PTO in New Orleans
 Parades, festivals and feasts for every day off
 Last Updated: Monday, November 16, 2026 1:55 PM 
 January. 14, 2025 
 --> 
 By Lauren Saizan 
 New Orleans is the ideal place to spend your paid time off, especially when you maximize it over holiday weekends. In New Orleans, every holiday weekend comes with some kind of festival or celebration, like the Gay Easter Parade, Greek Fest over Memorial Day Weekend, Bayou Classic over Thanksgiving Weekend, and of course, the holidays. Here are a few ideas for planning your 2027 trip to New Orleans featuring all the major festivals over holiday weekends to help you decide when to visit.

 Your 2027 PTO Calendar at a Glance
 New Year’s Day: Friday, Jan. 1 | Thursday, Dec. 31, 2026 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 MLK Day: Monday, Jan. 18 | Friday, Jan. 15 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Mardi Gras: Tuesday, Feb. 9 | Monday and Tuesday, Feb. 8-9 | 2 PTO = 4 days
 Presidents’ Day: Monday, Feb. 15 | Friday, Feb. 12 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Easter: Sunday, March 28 | Friday, March 26, and Monday, March 29 | 2 PTO = 4 days
 Memorial Day: Monday, May 31 | Friday, May 28 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Juneteenth: observed Friday, June 18 | Thursday, June 17 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Independence Day: observed Monday, July 5 | Friday, July 2 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Labor Day: Monday, Sept. 6 | Friday, Sept. 3 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Indigenous Peoples’ Day: Monday, Oct. 11 | Friday, Oct. 8 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Veterans Day: Thursday, Nov. 11 | Friday, Nov. 12 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Thanksgiving: Thursday, Nov. 25 | Friday, Nov. 26 | 1 PTO = 4 days
 Christmas to New Year’s: observed Friday, Dec. 24, and Friday, Dec. 31 | Monday-Thursday, Dec. 27-30 | 4 PTO = 10 days
 Editor's Note: These holidays assume a Monday-Friday schedule that follows federal holidays, plus a little lagniappe. Always check with your employer to determine which holidays are observed. 
 Justen Williams
 New Orleans City Park
 How to Maximize Your PTO in 2027
 Make the most of your vacation days in 2027 by planning around holidays and festival weekends. Thursday and Monday holidays offer some of the best opportunities to turn one or two PTO days into a four-day getaway. Mardi Gras Weekend does not fall on a holiday weekend this year but is worth the extra PTO. Christmas week offers the year's longest potential vacation stretch, while early hotel reservations are key for high-demand periods like Mardi Gras, Jazz Fest, and Thanksgiving.
 Winter Long Weekends in New Orleans  
 Carnival season through Presidents’ Day 
 Martin Luther King Jr. Day Weekend
 Jan 15-18 (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off)  
 The third Monday in January is Martin Luther King, Jr. Day. New Orleans has plenty of community gatherings and volunteer opportunities to commemorate the day. The  Ogden Museum of Southern Art   offers free admission plus art, crafts, and music in celebration of MLK Day.  New Orleans City Park  hosts an annual day of service on MLK Day. 
 MLK Weekend always falls during Carnival season . This means king cake season is in full swing and, depending on the year, parades may be rolling . Make it a long weekend and take that Friday before off, combining for a four-day trip to New Orleans. See our page on January in New Orleans here .

 Mardi Gras 2027
 Feb 6-9 (2 PTO Days = 4 Days Off) 
 While not falling over a federal holiday this year, coming down for Mardi Gras Weekend is always worth it! If you take two days off (Monday and Tuesday), you'll catch all the action including parades like Iris, Tucks, Endymion, Bacchus, Orpheus, Zulu, and Rex, plus festivities like the Zulu Lundi Gras Festival , Bourbon Street Awards , and more. Find our  Ultimate Mardi Gras Guide here for the ultimate inspiration. 
 Presidents' Day Weekend
 Feb 13-16 (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off) 
 President's Day Weekend once again falls over  Valentine's Day , and what city is more romantic than NOLA? Enjoy dinner reservations, walks through the French Quarter, and more with our  Romantic Itinerary . Since this falls after Mardi Gras, Lenten fish frys will be in full swing, as well as the start of crawfish season . Find where to get boiled seafood in NOLA here .
 Rebecca Todd
 Gay Easter Parade
 Spring Long Weekends and Festival Season 
 The year’s biggest PTO payoff 
 Easter Weekend 
 March 26-29 (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off)  
 Though not technically a federal holiday, Easter Weekend is an awesome time to visit New Orleans. On the Saturday of Easter Weekend, run the Crescent City Classic 10K . Then on Easter Day, head to the French Quarter for Easter parades, including the Gay Easter Parade . Dine on brunch and enjoy the beautiful springtime weather. See our page on things to do in March here and things to do in April here .
 Justen Williams
 The National WWII Museum
 Memorial Day  
 May 28-31 ( 1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off )  
 Memorial Day Weekend in New Orleans is spent by visiting the National WWII Museum , picnicking with friends , and enjoying the unofficial start of summer. Greek Fest is always held over Memorial Day Weekend, with Greek food, music, art, dancing, and a 5K. The festival takes place on Bayou St. John , where many people go kayaking in the summer months. 
 Justen Williams
 New Orleans Juneteenth Festival
 Summer Long Weekends 
 Cool festivals and summertime celebrations 
 Juneteenth National Independence Day 
 June 18-21  (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off)  
 New Orleans is rich in Black history, and special celebrations emerge for this federal holiday every year. Always on June 19, the New Orleans Juneteenth Festival commemorates the holiday in Congo Square with food, music, dancing and a drumming circle. Find more ways to commemorate Juneteenth in New Orleans here . 
 Cheryl Gerber
 Go Fourth on the River Fireworks Show
 Independence Day 
 July 2-5 (1  PTO Day = 4 Days Off)    
 Celebrate the Fourth of July in New Orleans with fireworks on the Mississippi River, plus food and music. Go Fourth on the River takes over the Riverwalk and Crescent Park with those festivities. Follow our Things to Do in July blog post here for more inspiration .
 Paul Broussard
 Southern Decadence
 Labor Day  
 Sept 3-6 (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off)  
 Labor Day Weekend in New Orleans is full of revelry as the summer comes to a close. Southern Decadence , a mash-up of New Orleans Pride and Gay Mardi Gras, has been a Labor Day weekend tradition in the  French Quarter  since 1972. Special events take place over six days, including the Southern Decadence Parade. Make sure to go to a drag or burlesque show while you’re in town. 
 Fall and Holiday Season Long Weekends 
 Cooler weather, festivals, and the holidays 
 Indigenous Peoples’ Day 
 Oct 8-11  (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off)  
 Just as it begins to really feel like fall, we celebrate Indigenous Peoples’ Day. In 2022, Our Voice Nuestra Voz, the United Houma Nation, and community members gathered at the New Orleans City Council to celebrate the city’s recognition of Indigenous People’s Day a holiday. Dive into the city’s history with a walking tour. Browse our tours page here .  
 October means a chill in the air with lots of festivals. Enjoy a piping hot bowl of gumbo and make sure to mark your calendar for one of our many October festivals . Also enjoy Oktoberfest at Deutsches Haus here and Hispanic Heritage Month celebrations here . Read more on fall travel here and October in New Orleans here . 
 Veterans Day 
 Nov 11-14 (1 PTO Day = 4 Days Off) 
 On Veterans Day, the National WWII Museum offers free admission for all veterans, plus a Veterans Day Commemoration Ceremony with a salute to all servicemembers, the presenting of awards, and the unveiling of special exhibits. Every weekend in November features a festival or major event, so follow our page on Things to Do in November here to see what's on tap.
 Cheryl Gerber
 Bayou Classic
 Thanksgiving Weekend
 Nov 25-29 (1 PTO Day = 5 Days Off)  
 Thanksgiving Day in New Orleans means food, food, and more food. Whether you come for the week or just for the weekend, you're bound to have a great time in the mild fall weather. Skip the cooking at home and  dine at a local restaurant . Feast on gumbo, seafood, and the traditional turkey and stuffing, plus bread pudding and more New Orleans classics.  
 If you're interested in getting active or just having a good time, check out the 5-mile Turkey Day Race in City Park . Head out to Easton Park in Mid-City for the  Human Horse Races , a family-friendly fundraiser where people dress as horses and race each other, all while raising money for a horse sanctuary. And we can't forget about Bayou Classic , an annual Thanksgiving Weekend tradition in NOLA with a football game, parade, Battle of the Bands, and more! Read our Ultimate Guide to the Bayou Classic here for more .
 Katie LaRocca
 Celebrate New Year's Eve in New Orleans
 Christmas and New Year's
 Dec 23 - Jan 2 (3 PTO Days = 11 Days Off)  
 While many offices are closed the week of Christmas, you can make a trip out of using just a few PTO Days if not. Around Christmas Day, enjoy lots of festivities with Holidays New Orleans Style . Enjoy lights in the park at Celebration in the Oaks , dining at a restaurant featuring a decadent Réveillon menu , ice skating and family fun at NOLA ChristmasFest , and more! Read about celebrating the Holidays New Orleans Style here . 
 Then for New Year's Eve, head down to Jackson Square for New Orleans Eve , a free concert featuring local musicians and fireworks at midnight. Make reservations to dine at a restaurant and find what's open here . Visit our page on New Year Eve in NOLA here .
 FAQs
 What are the best long weekends to visit New Orleans in 2027?
 Mardi Gras weekend, Jazz Fest, and Thanksgiving weekend are the biggest draws, and each takes only one or two PTO days. For the longest stretch, take Monday through Thursday off between Christmas and New Year’s to get 10 days off for four PTO days (assuming your office is closed on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve).
 How many PTO days do I need for Mardi Gras 2027?
 Mardi Gras Day is Tuesday, Feb. 9, 2027. Take Monday and Tuesday off and you get four days, from the final parade weekend through Lundi Gras and Mardi Gras Day. To catch Thursday night parades too, plan on four PTO days.
 When is Jazz Fest 2027?
 The New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival runs April 22-25 and April 29-May 2, 2027, at the Fair Grounds Race Course. Taking Thursday and Friday off for either weekend gives you a four-day trip.
 What can I do in New Orleans over Thanksgiving weekend?
 Many New Orleans restaurants serve Thanksgiving menus , so you can skip the cooking and book a table. The weekend also brings Bayou Classic, with its parade, Battle of the Bands and football game, plus the Turkey Day Race in City Park. Reserve dinner early.
 Is it worth visiting New Orleans on MLK weekend?
 Yes. By MLK weekend Carnival season is underway, king cake is in bakeries across the city and the weather is mild. Parade schedules shift each year, so check the parade calendar before you book.
 Do I need to book early for holiday weekends in New Orleans?
 For Mardi Gras, Jazz Fest, and Thanksgiving, yes. Hotels fill quickly on those weekends, so book as soon as your PTO is approved.
